plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Self-serve pay-as-you-go account, no platform fee; GPU quota may need a request.

caveats: Website blocked (403), use public Vultr plans API. Fractional GPU slices not equivalent to a full GPU. Listed plan may have no currently offered regions. API hourly vs monthly costs retained without assuming a cap policy.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

SKU check 2026-09-28 (API /v2/plans?type=all + vultr.com/pricing): Vultr sells NO single-GPU H100 VM - H100 is only the 8x HGX VM ($23.92/h in the API; website "starting at $2.300/GPU/hr") or 8x bare metal. 1x L40S ($1.671/h), 2x/4x L40S and 1x A100 80 GB PCIe ($2.397/h) exist but the API lists no deployable locations for any of them (flag stock).
Full-GPU VM rates are all-in (vCPU, RAM and local disk included) and encoded as the per-GPU price with vcpu_h = ram_gib_h = 0; disk beyond 0 GiB shows as unknown although each plan bundles 1.2-13 TB.
Billing caps: cloud GPU instances are billed up to 730 h/month, bare metal and other server types up to 672 h/month; stopped instances keep billing until destroyed.

fleet.verification: Consistent usage and positive billing history; request confirms profile, organization size and use case.
fleet.notes: Console Billing > Limits shows maximum instance count and total instance cost. Request Custom Limit Adjustment or support ticket; initial numeric caps, GPU-specific allowance and turnaround are not published in reviewed guidance.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Automatic Backups run automatically but you must take a snapshot manually.
snapshot_auto.note: Nothing is captured on stop; a stopped Cloud GPU keeps its disk and keeps billing ('an instance incurs normal charges as it would when active'). Optional scheduled Automatic Backups exist for Cloud GPU (daily/weekly etc. schedule, disk only) - scheduled, not stop-triggered.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Cloud GPU VMs only: POST /v2/snapshots {instance_id}, vultr-cli snapshot create, console. Disk only, no memory. New instances can boot from a snapshot (snapshot_id on create; snapshots usable across regions). NOT for GPU bare metal: 'No, snapshots are not available for Bare Metal instances.' $0.05/GB-month compressed.

harness_api.quote: Powerful GPU-accelerated cloud computing solutions for AI, machine learning, and graphics-intensive workloads with flexible provisioning options.
harness_api.note: Vultr Cloud GPU is a plain IaaS GPU VM/bare-metal product (Management, Connection, Networking, Features categories cover firewall/SSH/snapshots/backups/VPC - no agent-harness or code-execution SDK/API). Confirming the existing 'no' is outside what this product is: it's raw compute, not an agent-runtime layer.

egress_allowlist.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_allowlist.note: Firewall groups are inbound-only. The only provider-side egress control is topology: a VPC-only instance (no public IP) whose outbound path is a NAT Gateway; NAT Gateway firewall rules filter inbound port-forwarded traffic (source subnet/port), not destinations. No per-instance outbound allow/deny list.

egress_http_rules.quote: No, Vultr Firewall does not filter outgoing netwok traffic from your instance.
egress_http_rules.note: No outbound filtering at all, so no HTTP-level egress rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Vultr Firewall groups enable the creation of firewall rules to filter incoming traffic on an instance's public network interface.
ingress_rules.note: Firewall group rules by protocol/port/source IP-CIDR (IPv4/IPv6), attached per instance via API/CLI/Terraform. Also VPC-only 'Private Instance(s) behind NAT Gateway' deployment with no public IP, exposing ports only via NAT port-forward + NAT firewall rules.

guest_firewall.note: Cloud GPU is a full KVM VM with root (bare metal: whole server); iptables/nftables work. Firewall FAQ confirms instance-level firewall and Vultr Firewall both apply.

secret_proxy.quote: Powerful GPU-accelerated cloud computing solutions for AI, machine learning, and graphics-intensive workloads with flexible provisioning options.
secret_proxy.note: Same plain-IaaS product: docs categories (Management/Connection/Networking/Features) describe firewalls, SSH, snapshots, block storage, VPC - no credential-injecting secret proxy for instances. Secrets are supplied by the user via cloud-init/user-data or SSH like any VPS, so a 'no' fits what the product is.

volume_attach.quote: Yes, you can attach up to 16 Vultr Block Storage volumes to the same Vultr Cloud Compute instance.
volume_attach.note: Block Storage (NVMe min 1 GB, HDD min 40 GB), same-location, live attach, single-attach. Docs phrase attachment in terms of 'Cloud Compute instance'; Cloud GPU VMs use the same instances API but GPU eligibility is not stated explicitly (hence medium). Not for bare metal: 'No, Vultr Block Storage volumes do not support Vultr Bare Metal Servers.'

volume_shared.quote: Vultr File System is intended for clusters of CPU or GPU systems to share stored data between them
volume_shared.note: Vultr File System (VFS): virtiofs, read-write, 'you can attach multiple Vultr Cloud Compute instances to a single Vultr File System volume provided the instance and the volume are in the same Vultr location'; instance needs Memory Backing = Shared. Block Storage is single-attach.

isolation.note: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are full KVM virtual machines (the card's own top-level isolation field also says "vm"); the largest H100/L40S shapes are bare-metal passthrough nodes, but the modeled cloud-GPU product is KVM VM.

image_oci.quote: ISO images allow you to install a specific operating system on a Vultr VX1™ Cloud Compute instance. Custom ISOs enable you to deploy operating systems not available in the default Vultr installer list.
image_oci.note: Custom boot media is via ISO upload or a disk Snapshot, not a Docker/OCI image; no OCI-image boot path for Cloud GPU VMs was found.

docker_inside.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
docker_inside.note: Root/sudo access on a standard Linux KVM VM; Vultr's own docs and marketplace guides show installing and running Docker (including GPU containers with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit) on Cloud GPU instances.

desktop.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain GPU IaaS VM, no managed VNC/RDP desktop stream)

browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope

egress_ip_type.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
egress_ip_type.note: Standard Vultr datacenter public IPv4/IPv6 assigned to the instance; no residential/mobile IP offering.

ssh.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
ssh.note: Standard Linux VM provisioned with SSH keys, reachable via public IP like any Vultr Cloud Compute instance.

snapshot.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
snapshot.note: Disk/filesystem only, no memory/process state; on-demand only (no auto snapshot on stop). Not available for GPU bare metal.

fork.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
fork.note: No instance-clone API; the closest is manually snapshotting a disk and booting a new instance from that snapshot image, not a one-step fork. Vultr's 'fork' terminology only exists for Managed Databases, not compute/GPU instances.

fork_running.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
fork_running.note: No cloning-a-running-machine capability for Cloud GPU compute instances.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of the instance state that includes the file system and disk contents.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots are disk-only (no memory/process state), and there is no fork feature for compute instances at all.

pause_resume.quote: an instance incurs normal charges as it would when active
pause_resume.note: Only stop/start is offered (vultr-cli instance stop halts without terminating), and stopped instances keep billing until destroyed; there is no pause with reduced/paused billing.

wake_on_request.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (always-on IaaS VM/bare metal, no request-triggered wake mechanism)

auto_stop_idle.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no idle-detection auto-stop found in docs (billing caps documented are monthly hour caps, not idle timeouts)

live_resize.quote: Resizing an instance activates a new plan with more vCPUs, RAM, and storage to match your needs.
live_resize.note: PATCH /v2/instances changes the plan of the same instance ID/disk without recreating it (documented for Cloud/Optimized Compute instances using the same instances API as Cloud GPU); a reboot is likely involved but the machine is not destroyed/recreated.

agent_harnesses.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
agent_harnesses.note: No preinstalled/templated coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) for Cloud GPU instances; only generic GPU/ML marketplace apps.

own_agent_api.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
own_agent_api.note: Vultr has no first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API; it is IaaS compute.

mcp_server.quote: connecting a coding agent through Microsandbox's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so the agent creates and uses its own sandboxes on demand
mcp_server.note: Vultr docs show third-party tutorials for running/hosting MCP servers on Vultr instances (e.g. Microsandbox, FastMCP), but Vultr itself does not ship an MCP server for controlling its own sandboxes/instances.

lang_python.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
lang_python.note: Not baked into the base GPU image by default, but Vultr's Marketplace offers one-click Python application deployment and most default Linux distro images ship python3; root access lets you install any runtime.

lang_node.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
lang_node.note: Vultr Marketplace offers a one-click Node.js application deployment; root access lets you install Node.js on any base image.

public_ipv4.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are KVM virtual machines with full root access
public_ipv4.note: Standard Vultr Cloud Compute/GPU instances are provisioned with a public IPv4 address by default (VPC-only private deployment is an opt-in alternative).

inbound_https.quote: Vultr Firewall groups enable the creation of firewall rules to filter incoming traffic on an instance's public network interface.
inbound_https.note: Instance has a public IPv4 and open inbound firewall rules can be created for port 443/HTTPS; you run and terminate TLS yourself (no managed HTTPS gateway included, but reachability is provider-supported).

static_egress_ip.quote: reserved_ipv4 - (Optional) The ID of the floating IP to use as the main IP of this server. See Reserved IPs
static_egress_ip.note: The instance's public IPv4 stays fixed for the life of the instance, and Vultr Reserved (floating) IPs can also be attached/moved between instances for a stable address.

windows.note: Every Cloud GPU plan in the Vultr plans API lists Linux as the only supported OS; no Windows Server option for Cloud GPU.

macos.quote: Vultr Cloud GPU offers dedicated GPU-accelerated compute instances for AI/ML training, inference, and high-performance workloads.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Vultr does not sell macOS machines at all)

arm64.note: not offered: Vultr's ARM64 Cloud Compute is a separate x86-only-independent product line; the Cloud GPU catalog (vcg/vdm/bare-metal) contains no ARM64 shapes.

self_host.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Vultr is a managed public cloud provider, not self-hostable software.

byoc.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Vultr runs its own datacenters, it is not deployed into a customer's cloud account.

open_source.quote: Vultr Global Cloud Hosting - Brilliantly Fast SSD VPS Cloud Servers.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Vultr's core cloud platform is proprietary.

soc2.quote: The table lists each data center location alongside the certifications it holds, including SOC 2, SOC 1, HITRUST, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, NIST800-53, SOC 3, HIPAA / HiTech, and ISO 14001/50001.
soc2.note: SOC 2 report downloadable via Trust & Compliance center (clickwrapped PDF).

hipaa.quote: including SOC 2, SOC 1, HITRUST, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001, NIST800-53, SOC 3, HIPAA / HiTech, and ISO 14001/50001
hipaa.note: HIPAA / HiTech listed as a data-center compliance certification available for applicable locations; not confirmed whether Vultr signs a BAA for Cloud GPU specifically.

sso.quote: Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users in your organization sign in to Vultr through an external identity provider instead of a Vultr password. Vultr supports SSO through OpenID Connect (OIDC), and works with any OIDC-compliant identity provider.
sso.note: Organization-level SSO via OIDC, configurable in the Vultr Console.

eu_data_residency.note: Vultr operates multiple EU regions (Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Paris, Warsaw, Madrid); GPU plan availability per-region varies but EU regions exist for compute generally.

max_session_h.quote: an instance incurs normal charges as it would when active
max_session_h.note: A running Cloud GPU VM has no maximum session duration; it runs until you stop/destroy it (subject to monthly billing hour caps documented separately, which are billing caps not runtime limits).

nested_virt.quote: You can access a Vultr Cloud GPU instance depending on its operating system. Use SSH or the Vultr Console for Linux instances and the Remote Desktop Protocol for Windows instances.
nested_virt.note: Vultr Cloud GPU instances are standard KVM virtual machines (the card's own isolation field is qemu-kvm). Vultr's Cloud GPU and Cloud Compute FAQ/feature docs describe SSH/console access, snapshots, firewalls, backups, VPC, etc., but neither the Cloud GPU FAQ, Cloud Compute FAQ, nor the general docs llms.txt index mention nested virtualization, /dev/kvm passthrough, or running VMs inside an instance anywhere. No official page claims the guest CPU exposes VMX/SVM. Consistent with the common pattern for shared-host KVM cloud VMs (as opposed to bare metal, which Vultr sells separately), where the hypervisor does not expose virtualization extensions to the guest. Could not find an explicit official statement either confirming or denying it, so this is inferred rather than directly quoted.
